description.en:
An ontology for representing historical place knowledge as attestations:
        bundles of evidence linking SpatialEntities (settlements, routes,
        networks, administrative units, regions and other entities whose
        identity is bound up with space) to Names, Geometries, Timespans,
        Types, PropertyValues and Authorities with full provenance.

        Developed by the Pelagios Network's Place Working Group, led by the
        Institute for Spatial History Innovation (ISHI), University of Pittsburgh.

        PLATO formalises the WHG v4 data model, in which the Attestation is
        the fundamental unit of contributed knowledge. The Linked Places
        Format (LPF) is defined as its single-object-attestation profile:
        every LPF element corresponds to one attestation linking one entity
        to one name, type, geometry or related entity, so existing LPF files
        remain valid. The use cases of Linked Traces are accommodated within
        the same model.

comment.en:
A spatial representation of a SpatialEntity's extent or location. Geometries
        are independent, reusable entities. The same Geometry may be referenced
        by multiple Attestations across different SpatialEntities or time periods.

        Note: GeometryCollection is not supported in some graph database
        implementations. For heterogeneous geometry sets (e.g., both point and
        polygon), use multiple Geometry entities linked through separate
        attestations.

A toponym or appellation for a SpatialEntity. Names are independent, reusable
        entities. The association between a Name and a SpatialEntity is always mediated
        by an Attestation, which provides temporal scope and provenance.

One attestation's use of one Authority: the qualified form of
        plato:sourced_by. Carries what is true of this citation rather than
        of the source or of the attestation: the locator within the work
        (page, folio, column, table cell, entry), and whether the attribution
        was stated in the source or inferred editorially. It carries no date.
        The date of a witness belongs on the Source (plato:source_timespan)
        and the date of the claim on the Attestation's Timespan.

        An attestation resting on several sources has several Citations,
        each with its own locator. Where there is nothing to say about the
        citation, plato:sourced_by alone is sufficient.

An assertion that two SpatialEntities refer to the same real-world entity.
        Carries its own provenance (who asserted it, on what basis),
        certainty (how confident the assertion is), and identity semantics
        (exactMatch, closeMatch, related).

        Identity relations are distinct from scholarly entity-to-entity
        relations, which describe substantive historical relationships
        between different entities. They are also distinct from Candidates,
        which are algorithm-generated candidates not yet confirmed by
        human review.

A mutable, versioned workspace of SpatialEntities and their associated
        Attestations, owned by a contributor or team. Replaces the WHG v3
        concepts of Dataset, Dataset Collection, and Place Collection.
        A Gazetteer can be incrementally edited, enriched, and corrected
        without re-ingestion.

A person, team, or automated process that creates attestations.
        Aligned with both foaf:Agent and prov:Agent for provenance
        chain-of-custody tracking.

        Contributors should be identified using persistent identifiers where
        possible. For persons, ORCID (https://orcid.org/) is strongly
        recommended and may be required by specific implementations. ORCID
        identifiers should use the full URI format (https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000)
        rather than just the numeric portion, as ORCID is particular about
        proper URI formatting for linked data interoperability.

        For organizations, ROR (https://ror.org/) or ISNI identifiers are
        recommended. Proper identification ensures accurate attribution,
        enables citation, and supports research assessment.

A vocabulary entry defining a semantic relationship between SpatialEntities:
        'capital_of', 'successor_to', 'connected_by_trade_route_to', etc.
        Carries a label, an inverse label, and domain/range constraints.
        This allows the vocabulary of historical relationships to grow
        without modifying the core ontology.

An organization to which a Contributor is affiliated. This is a
        lightweight class defined primarily to avoid ambiguity in ontology
        visualizations. Organizations can be further described using properties
        from FOAF, schema.org, or other ontologies.

        Organizations should use persistent identifiers where possible:
        - ROR (Research Organization Registry): https://ror.org/
        - ISNI (International Standard Name Identifier)
        - Wikidata QIDs

A collection-level authority: a published gazetteer, a contributed
        dataset, or an external authority corpus (GeoNames, Wikidata, TGN,
        OSM, Pleiades). Carries metadata such as title, version, publisher,
        licence, and URI.

An entity whose identity is bound up with space, whether its spatial
        extent is attested directly, applies notionally (as with the region to
        which a period applies), or is derived from its constituents (as with a
        collection). A SpatialEntity need not have any attested geometry: lost,
        imagined and unlocated entities are admissible.

        What kind of entity it is (settlement, route, region, administrative
        unit, period and so on) is not fixed by the class. It is established by
        Type attestations, so a classification is a claim rather than an axiom.

        SpatialEntities are not defined by any single attestation. They are the
        point of convergence for many attestations from different sources,
        periods and contributors.

        A SpatialEntity is not a place, and PLATO defines no Place class.
        "Place" carries several meanings in the gazetteer community, and
        which of them, if any, corresponds to a SpatialEntity is contested;
        the ontology does not settle it. Neither a SpatialEntity nor any set
        of attestations or of SpatialEntities is a place by virtue of this
        ontology. Where the word appears in this document it is used
        informally, for whatever a source is talking about.

A classification or category for a SpatialEntity, typically drawn from a
        controlled vocabulary such as the Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus
        (AAT). Types are independent, reusable entities.

An algorithm-generated match candidate between two SpatialEntities, produced
        by the PLACE clustering engine. Candidates carry a similarity score,
        algorithm version, and review status. They are explicitly not
        IdentityRelations — they become IdentityRelations only when confirmed
        by a human reviewer (linked back via plato:promoted_from).

Abstract superclass for all reference entities that provide provenance
        or semantic grounding for attestations. Subtypes include Source,
        Dataset, Period, RelationType, and CertaintyLevel.

A defined level of certainty for use in attestations, allowing
        projects to standardise their confidence vocabulary.

A quantitative or descriptive attribute of a SpatialEntity, expressed as a
        property drawn from an external vocabulary together with its value.
        Covers the many things a historical source says that are neither a
        name, a location, a period nor a classification — populations,
        valuations, elevations, recurrence rules for markets and fairs.

        The property itself is identified by URI rather than enumerated here,
        so the vocabulary stays open and delegated (Wikidata properties,
        CIDOC-CRM, project vocabularies), in the same way that Type delegates
        its classifications to AAT.

        Values may be literals (with a datatype and optional unit) or
        structured objects whose shape is declared by plato:value_type. As a
        facet node, a PropertyValue may carry the qualification properties
        (certainty, fuzziness) like any other.

        Where the value is itself an entity, use a entity-to-entity relation
        instead; this class is for attributes, not relationships.

A bundle of evidence asserting that a particular SpatialEntity had a particular
        Name, Geometry, Type, or combination thereof, during a particular
        Timespan, according to a particular Authority. The Attestation node
        carries only metadata; its semantic content is defined entirely by its
        outgoing relationships.

        IMPORTANT: Attestations are document nodes in the graph, not edges.
        They are instances of plato:Attestation (a class), not instances of
        owl:ObjectProperty. This design enables meta-attestations and full
        provenance tracking.

A temporal interval with start and end bounds. Timespans are
        independent, reusable entities that may be shared across multiple
        Attestations. Precision and uncertainty are expressed through
        the start and end bound properties. Aligned with W3C Time Ontology
        and compatible with PeriodO period definitions.

A citable source of evidence: a manuscript, chronicle, tax record,
        map, scholarly article, or other document. Sources are the primary
        provenance anchor for attestations. A Source may reference its parent
        Dataset via plato:partOf.

A thematic or organisational grouping of Gazetteers (e.g.
        'EMEW — Gazetteer of Early Modern England and Wales').

A named historical period (e.g. 'Byzantine', 'Early Modern'),
        optionally linked to PeriodO or defined locally. Includes temporal
        bounds for period-based querying.

Human-readable label for this timespan (e.g., 'Byzantine period',
        'Early Bronze Age', 'Ming Dynasty'). Particularly useful for named
        periods referenced across multiple attestations.

Structured metadata for network-type attestations. Can encode
        information about trade goods, flow direction, capacity, frequency,
        or other properties of network connections. Format is implementation-
        specific (JSON recommended) but should be documented in the gazetteer's
        metadata.
URI or identifier in a controlled vocabulary (e.g. AAT).

Extended Date/Time Format (EDTF) representation of this timespan.
        Provides standardized string encoding for interchange with systems
        using EDTF. Optional but recommended for interoperability with library
        and archival systems. Example: '1453-05-29/1453-05-29' or '1450~/1453~'
        for approximate dates.

The original label as given in the contributing source, before
        vocabulary mapping. For a structured PropertyValue this preserves the
        unparsed original — 'Monday after Whitsun, 3 days' — which is what a
        future reader will want to check against the document.

Whether the attribution of the evidence to the cited source was
        stated by the source or resolved editorially. Should point to a
        concept in a SKOS concept scheme. The starter concepts are:

        - plato:AttributionStated: the source is named where the form
          occurs. The default, and usually omitted.
        - plato:AttributionInferred: the source was given as 'ibidem' or
          'idem' and resolved by an editor, so the attribution is inferred
          rather than stated. Not marginal: about one attestation in twenty
          in the English Place-Name Society corpus.

        A statement about the citation, not about the form, which is why it
        lives here and not in plato:occurrence_context.

Links an Attestation to a Type classification it assigns to the SpatialEntity.
        An attestation may assert multiple types or no type at all.

Organizational affiliation of the contributor. Links to a
        plato:Organization entity, which can be further described using
        FOAF, schema.org, or other ontology properties. Organizations
        should ideally use persistent identifiers (ROR, ISNI, etc.).

        For simple cases, use contributor_affiliation_string for free-text
        affiliation names.

The value, where it is a literal: a number, a string, a date. Use
        plato:value_json instead where the value is structured.

What the name denotes. The list is open: 'toponym' (place name),
        'chrononym' (period or era name), 'ethnonym' (people or ethnic
        group), 'demonym' (inhabitants), 'odonym' (street or road name) and
        'hydronym' (water body) are the starter values, and a project may
        add others ('oronym', 'hagionym') provided it documents them in its
        gazetteer metadata. Multiple types are possible (a name that
        functions as both toponym and ethnonym). plato.schema.json carries
        the same open list; earlier releases closed it there, and the two
        serialisations now agree.

        This classifies the referent, not the status of the form. Whether a
        string is an attested spelling, an editorial headword or a derived
        search form is a property of the attestation (plato:form_status),
        because the same string can have a different status in different
        attestations.

Links an Attestation to the Authority (typically a Source or Dataset)
        that grounds it. This provides the provenance chain for the attestation.

        Semantically equivalent to PROV-O's prov:wasDerivedFrom, indicating the
        authority is the origin of the attested knowledge. We don't use formal
        rdfs:subPropertyOf to avoid importing PROV-O's domain/range constraints
        which conflict with PLATO's class structure.

        This is the direct form. Where the citation itself has something to
        say (a page or folio, an attribution resolved from 'ibidem'), use
        plato:has_citation to a Citation node that cites the Authority.
        sourced_by is declared as the property chain has_citation o cites, so
        a reasoner derives it from a Citation; data intended for consumers
        without a reasoner should assert it directly as well.

Well-Known Text representation of the geometry, following OGC/ISO
        standards. Used for GeoSPARQL queries and RDF serialization.
        Supports Point, LineString, Polygon, MultiPoint, MultiLineString,
        MultiPolygon.

Link to a PeriodO period definition (https://perio.do/). When a timespan
        corresponds to a standardized period in PeriodO, this property enables
        alignment and allows PLATO to inherit PeriodO's temporal bounds, spatial
        coverage, and cultural context. Example: 'https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p06v8w4rb38'

The authority namespace for this SpatialEntity (e.g. 'geonames', 'wikidata',
        'tgn', 'osm', 'pleiades', 'whg'). Authority-sourced SpatialEntities carry
        their origin namespace; contributed SpatialEntities that cannot be linked to
        any authority receive the 'whg' namespace.

Links a facet node to its anchor entity, indicating that this
        facet is defined relationally rather than absolutely. The anchor
        is typically a SpatialEntity, Period, or another facet (Name, Timespan, etc.).

        Common patterns:
        - Spatial relativity: "20km east of Nanjing" (anchor is a SpatialEntity)
        - Temporal relativity: "during the reign of Justinian" (anchor is a Period)
        - Name relativity: "also known as Rome" (anchor is another Name)
Links a Gazetteer to a GazetteerGroup.

Role of the contributor in the project or gazetteer. Examples:
        'principal_investigator', 'data_curator', 'student_researcher',
        'automated_process', 'external_contributor'. Helps understand the
        context and authority of contributions.
Links a Source to its parent Dataset.
Links a Gazetteer to an Attestation contributed within it.
Human-readable label for this type.

Free-text explanation of the certainty assessment: quality of
        evidence, degree of scholarly consensus, reliability of source
        (e.g. 'manuscript partially illegible', 'coordinates extrapolated
        from itinerary distances'). Applies wherever certainty does.

The semantic strength of the identity assertion:
        'exactMatch'  — the two SpatialEntities are unambiguously the same entity.
        'closeMatch'  — the two SpatialEntities are believed to be the same entity
                        but with some residual ambiguity (e.g. differing
                        granularity, overlapping but not identical scope).
        'related'     — the two SpatialEntities are closely associated but may not
                        be strictly identical (e.g. a settlement and its
                        administrative district, or successive phases of
                        a site that might or might not constitute continuity).

Free-text explanation of the evidence or reasoning supporting
        this identity assertion (e.g. 'coordinates within 500m and
        name forms are cognate', 'identified by contributor during
        reconciliation review', 'confirmed via TGN cross-reference').

Where in the cited work the evidence sits: 'p. 412', 'f. 12v', 'Table
        VI, col. 3, row 88', 's.v. Athlone', 'no. xix'. An uninterpreted
        string, deliberately: sources locate themselves inconsistently, and
        normalising the value would destroy exactly the information it is
        there to carry. The same position and shape as PeriodO's source
        locator.

        A property of this citation, not of the source: one Source for a
        printed gazetteer, a different locator on each attestation drawn
        from it. Not to be confused with the spatial sense of 'locator' in
        the plato:geometry_role comment, a proxy point standing in for an
        entity.

Links a meta-Attestation to the Attestation it comments on or relates to.
        Used with plato:has_meta_type to specify the nature of the relationship.

        Example: A meta-attestation might assert that one source's geometry
        attestation contradicts another source's geometry attestation for the
        same SpatialEntity.

ISO 15924 script code (e.g., 'Arab' for Arabic script, 'Latn' for
        Latin script, 'Hant' for Traditional Han characters). Important for
        names that may appear in multiple scripts.

A structured value serialised as JSON, whose shape is declared by
        plato:value_type. Use plato:value_literal instead for scalar values.

Links an IdentityRelation to the Candidate from which it was
        promoted, preserving the algorithmic provenance. Optional:
        identity relations can also be created directly by human
        assertion without a prior Candidate.

What this geometry depicts, as distinct from how precisely it is known
        (plato:spatial_precision) or where its indexing point falls
        (plato:repr_point). A SpatialEntity may be attested with several geometries at
        once — a built extent, the location of a specific central feature, a
        proxy standing in for the whole, the anchor of a map label — and without
        a declared role a consumer cannot tell them apart, nor state which one
        an analysis used.

        Should point to a concept in a SKOS concept scheme (e.g. plato:Extent,
        plato:FeaturePoint, plato:RepresentativePoint, plato:LabelAnchor,
        plato:Itinerary). Using URIs rather than free text lets gazetteers that
        record geometry differently be compared.

        Note that role is orthogonal to precision: a proxy locator may be
        surveyed to the metre and still not depict the SpatialEntity it stands for. A
        parish church's coordinates contributed as a locator for a town are a
        representative point of high precision, not an imprecise feature point.

The name of the contributor (person, team, or automated process).
        For persons, should be the full name as preferred by the contributor.
        For teams, the team name. For automated processes, a descriptive name.

Confidence in the identity assertion, from 0.0 to 1.0. This is
        the epistemic certainty of the asserter, distinct from identity_type
        which describes the semantic nature of the relationship.
        A closeMatch can have high certainty ('I'm confident these are
        close but not exact') and an exactMatch can have low certainty
        ('I think they're identical but I'm not sure').

The Authority (Source or Dataset) that provides evidence for
        this identity assertion, if any.

Numeric precision indicator in years. For example, a decade-level
        precision would have value 10, century-level would be 100. Enables
        computational comparison of precision across timespans.
The agent who made or confirmed this identity assertion.

Epistemic certainty, from 0.0 (completely uncertain) to 1.0
        (completely certain). On an Attestation it is the contributor's
        confidence in the bundle as a whole. On a facet node (Name, Geometry,
        Timespan, Type, PropertyValue) it is the confidence in that value
        alone, and may differ from the attestation's overall certainty.
        Certainty reflects the limits of evidence: better evidence could in
        principle raise it. Distinct from fuzziness (the referent has no
        sharp boundary) and from spatial_precision (how finely a location
        is specified). No rdfs:domain, so it can qualify any node.

The Authority (a Source or a Dataset) this Citation uses. Exactly one
        per Citation: an attestation resting on two sources has two
        Citations.
The first SpatialEntity in an identity assertion.

Links a Period authority to its temporal extent, represented as a
        Timespan node. Used for locally-defined periods or when more detailed
        temporal modeling is needed than provided by external period definitions.

Convex hull of the geometry as WKT Polygon. Used for quick spatial
        filtering before more expensive exact geometry operations. Optional
        but recommended for complex geometries.

URI declaring the shape of a structured value, so that a consumer can
        tell whether it understands the value before attempting to read it.
        Omitted for literal values.

        Not every attribute a source states is scalar. A market's trading day
        — 'the Monday after Whitsun, for three days' — is a recurrence rule
        anchored to a moveable feast, and flattening it to a string would
        reproduce the loss this class exists to prevent. The ontology stays
        agnostic about such shapes: it records which shape is in use and
        leaves the definition to the vocabulary that owns it.

Free-text notes providing additional context about this attestation.
        Can include transcriptions, translations, editorial comments, or
        other information that doesn't fit structured fields.

Precision qualifier for this geometry: 'exact' (surveyed or GPS),
        'approximate' (estimated from maps or descriptions), 'uncertain'
        (multiple possible locations), 'historical_approximate' (based on
        historical sources with inherent imprecision). Multiple values
        possible for heterogeneous geometries.
Datatype of the literal value (e.g. xsd:integer, xsd:decimal, xsd:string).

The earliest possible end date for this timespan. Together with
        end_latest, defines the uncertainty range for when the interval ended.
        May be null for unknown or deliberately open-end intervals.

A single representative point (centroid, label point, or best
        estimate) for spatial indexing and distance queries. Stored as WKT
        Point. Required for all geometries to enable spatial search.

The earliest possible start date for this timespan. Together with
        start_latest, defines the uncertainty range for when the interval began.
        Use ISO 8601 format (e.g., '1453-05-29') or integer year for year-level
        precision. May be null for unknown or deliberately open-beginning intervals.

Boolean flag indicating that the start of this interval is deliberately
        unspecified (not merely unknown). True for intervals like 'everything
        before 1453' or 'prehistory until...'. Distinct from null start_earliest,
        which indicates unknown start. Aligns with PeriodO's OpenBeginningInterval.

The agent (person, team, or process) who created this attestation.

        Semantically equivalent to PROV-O's prov:wasAttributedTo for provenance
        tracking. We don't use formal rdfs:subPropertyOf to avoid importing
        PROV-O's domain/range constraints. Distinct from sourced_by, which
        indicates the historical source being cited.

BCP 47 language tag for this name (e.g., 'ar' for Arabic, 'zh-Hans'
        for Simplified Chinese). Recommended: use ISO 639-3 three-letter codes
        within BCP 47 for better granularity (e.g., 'ara', 'cmn').

Boolean flag indicating that the end of this interval is deliberately
        unspecified (not merely unknown). True for ongoing periods like 'Modern
        era (1800-present)' or situations where the end does not exist. Aligns
        with PeriodO's OpenEndInterval.
Publication status: 'draft' or 'published'.
Inverse label (e.g. 'has_capital').
A formatted citation string for this source.

Contact email address for the contributor. Useful for collaboration
        and correspondence about contributed data.

URI of the unit of measurement, where the value has one — a QUDT unit
        or a Wikidata unit item. Omitted for counts and dimensionless values.

GeoJSON representation of the geometry. Used for web mapping
        applications and LPF export. Should be a valid GeoJSON geometry
        object (not a Feature or FeatureCollection).

Free-text explanation of the nature of ontological fuzziness
        (e.g. 'regional boundary was never formally demarcated',
        'name used inconsistently across contemporary sources',
        'transition was gradual rather than a discrete event').

Compass bearing from the anchor, in degrees (0–360).
        Primarily used for relative geometries: '90' means east of
        the anchor. May carry its own certainty or fuzziness.
Links a Gazetteer to a SpatialEntity it contains.
Forward label for the relationship (e.g. 'capital_of').

Links an Attestation to a Citation: its qualified use of one
        Authority, with a locator and an attribution status. An attestation
        may have several, one per source it rests on.

Geographic or cultural region to which this period applies.
        Free text or URI to a place/region. Useful because periods like
        'Medieval' have different temporal bounds in different regions.

The name string itself in its original script. This is the primary
        property of a Name entity. Required for all Name instances.

Original coordinate reference system. Typically 'EPSG:4326' (WGS84),
        but may reference historical or custom CRS identifiers for historical
        maps. Enables proper interpretation of coordinate values.

The latest possible start date for this timespan. For certain dates,
        this equals start_earliest. For uncertain dates, defines the end of
        the uncertainty range for when the interval began.

Distance from the anchor, in metres. Primarily used for
        relative geometries. May carry its own certainty or fuzziness.

The latest possible end date for this timespan. For certain dates,
        this equals end_earliest. For uncertain dates, defines the end of
        the uncertainty range for when the interval ended.
Valid subject type for this relation.

Vector embedding for phonetic similarity search. Typically a
        256-dimensional vector generated from the name's phonetic form,
        enabling fuzzy matching and transliteration-variant detection.
        Format is implementation-specific but should be documented in
        gazetteer metadata. WHG v4 uses Symphonym embeddings.

Temporal granularity of the end bound. Values: 'year', 'decade',
        'century', 'era', 'geological_period'.

The nature of a meta-attestation's relationship to its target attestation.
        Should reference a controlled vocabulary concept defining the relationship
        type. Standard values include:

        - 'contradicts': asserts the target attestation is incorrect
        - 'supports': provides additional evidence for the target attestation
        - 'supersedes': replaces the target attestation with newer information
        - 'refines': provides more precise information than the target
        - 'challenges': questions the target attestation's validity
        - 'bundles': groups the target with other related attestations

        Using SKOS concepts rather than strings enables vocabulary management
        and multilingual labels.

A controlled-vocabulary term describing the relative relationship
        when bearing and distance are not applicable or not sufficient.
        Should point to a concept in a SKOS concept scheme (e.g.
        plato:Near, plato:Within, plato:Beyond, plato:UpstreamOf,
        plato:BetweenXAndY, plato:DuringReignOf, plato:VariantOf).
        Using URIs rather than free text enables machine reconciliation
        across gazetteers that describe relativity differently.

Links an Attestation to a Name it asserts for the SpatialEntity. An attestation
        may assert multiple names (e.g., primary name and variants) or no name
        at all (e.g., geometry-only attestations).

Specifies the semantic type of a entity-to-entity relationship
        attested by an Attestation. References a RelationType authority
        which defines the relationship's label, inverse, and domain/range
        constraints. Examples: 'capital_of', 'successor_to',
        'connected_by_trade_route_to'.

        The extensible vocabulary pattern allows new relationship types to
        be added as Authority records without modifying the ontology.

This Source is a copy, transcript, edition, calendar or confirmation
        of that one. A later cartulary copy of a charter, an inspeximus, or a
        printed edition of a manuscript is a Source of its own, with its own
        source_timespan, derived_from the document it transmits. An
        attestation should cite the Source it was actually read in; the chain
        of derived_from links records what that Source transmits. The kind of
        derivation (copy, edition, calendar, inspeximus) is not yet
        distinguished; a sub-property or a small vocabulary can be added when
        a project needs it.

Links an Attestation to a PropertyValue it asserts of the SpatialEntity — a
        population, a valuation, an elevation, a market's trading day. An
        attestation may assert several properties or none.

        These are among the commonest things a source says about an entity, and
        they carry exactly the provenance and temporal scoping the attestation
        pattern exists to handle: a population figure is a claim, by a named
        source, about one SpatialEntity, over a Timespan, with a certainty. The
        attestation's own timespans scope the property as they scope every
        other facet in the bundle.

Links an Attestation to the Timespan during which the attested
        properties (name, geometry, type) were applicable. Distinct from
        the attestation's creation date: this is the historical timespan
        being asserted, not when the assertion was made.
Valid object type for this relation.

Links an Attestation to the SpatialEntity it is about. Every attestation must
        have exactly one subject entity. This is the primary entity being
        described by the bundled name, geometry, timespan, and type assertions.

        Functional property: each attestation has exactly one subject entity.

Ordering index for attestations in routes or itineraries. Defines
        the position of this attestation in an ordered sequence. Used when
        the SpatialEntity being attested (via attests_about) is a Route or Itinerary.
        Lower numbers come first in the sequence.

The status of the name form this attestation contributes: read in the
        cited source, chosen by the cited authority, or derived by the
        contributing project. Should point to a concept in a SKOS concept
        scheme. The starter concepts are:

        - plato:Attested: a form read in the cited source. The default, and
          usually omitted.
        - plato:Headword: the editorial or preferred form under which the
          cited authority files the entry ('Bunsty Hundred'). A scholarly
          decision rather than a reading, and typically the form users search
          for. Another authority may choose differently, which is why it is a
          sourced attestation and not a label on the SpatialEntity.
        - plato:Normalised: a form derived from an attested one for matching
          or search ('Bunstow(e)' resolved to 'Bunstowe'), attested by no
          source and carrying no independent evidential value. It may point
          to the attestation it was derived from through a meta-attestation.
        - plato:Reconstructed: a form inferred but not attested, the
          philologists' asterisked form.

        A different axis from plato:name_type, which classifies what the name
        denotes: a headword is still a toponym. It sits on the Attestation,
        not on the Name, because the same string can be a reading in one
        attestation and a headword in another. The WHG ingestion prototype
        reached the same placement independently: its preferred-name flag is
        on the attestation, not on the toponym record.

The number of times the attested form occurs in the cited source or
        passage: the '(3 X)' of a place-name survey. A count of occurrences
        of the form in this source, not of independent sources. It belongs to
        the attestation, not to the Name, which may occur elsewhere.

Ontological fuzziness: a measure of how inherently vague or
        indeterminate the facet's referent is, from 0.0 (crisp, sharply
        bounded) to 1.0 (maximally vague). Distinct from certainty:
        fuzziness is a property of the thing itself, not of our knowledge
        of it. A regional boundary that was never precisely defined has
        high fuzziness regardless of how much evidence we have.

Additional persistent identifier for the contributor. Can be used
        for identifiers other than ORCID, such as:
        - ISNI (International Standard Name Identifier)
        - VIAF (Virtual International Authority File)
        - Wikidata QID (for persons or organizations)
        - Internal system identifiers

        When using this property, specify the identifier type in the value
        (e.g., "ISNI:0000000121032683" or "VIAF:12345678").

Link to a PeriodO period definition for this Period authority.
        When present, indicates this Period aligns with a standardized PeriodO
        definition. The PeriodO record provides authoritative temporal bounds,
        spatial extent, and cultural context. Example: 'https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p06v8w4rb38'

URI of the property in an external vocabulary — a Wikidata property,
        a CIDOC-CRM property, or a project vocabulary term (e.g.
        <https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Property:P1082> for population).
        Keeping the vocabulary external rather than enumerating attributes in
        this ontology is what allows the model to carry attributes it has
        never heard of.

Romanized (Latin-script) form of the name for searchability and
        display in contexts requiring ASCII. Should specify transliteration
        system used via plato:transliteration_system.

Human-readable label for this period (e.g., 'Byzantine period',
        'Han Dynasty', 'Early Bronze Age'). Distinct from authority_title,
        which may be more formal.

Timestamp when this attestation was last modified. Enables tracking
        of editorial changes and versioning.

The capacity in which the attested form occurs in the source. Should
        point to a concept in a SKOS concept scheme. The starter concepts are:

        - plato:Direct: the form refers to the SpatialEntity directly. The
          default, and usually omitted.
        - plato:InPersonalName: the form occurs only as an element of a
          personal name, a surname or by-name such as 'Willelmus de
          Bonestou'. This is the '(p)' of the place-name surveys, and it is
          weaker evidence for the name's currency, and for the entity's
          existence, than a direct attestation. Nothing else in the record
          distinguishes Bonestou the hundred from de Bonestou the man.
        - plato:InFieldName: the form survives only as an element of a later
          minor name, such as a field name.

        The editorially resolved 'ibidem' of the surveys is not an occurrence
        context. It is a statement about the citation, and belongs on the
        Citation as plato:attribution_status.

        Not a certainty. A '(p)' attestation may be entirely certain as an
        attestation; what differs is the kind of evidence it constitutes, and
        folding that into a lower plato:certainty would discard the reason.

When this Source, as a document, was produced: the date of the
        manuscript, the compilation of the cartulary, the publication of the
        edition. Distinct from the Timespan an attestation asserts, which
        dates the claim rather than the witness. An annal for 921 read in a
        manuscript written c. 925 has an attested timespan of 921 and a
        source timespan of c. 925. Reuses Timespan, so an approximate date
        is start_earliest 915, end_latest 935, timespan_label 'c. 925'. The
        same move as plato:has_timespan on a Period.

Temporal granularity of the start bound. Values: 'year', 'decade',
        'century', 'era', 'geological_period'. This describes the resolution
        of the date specification, distinct from certainty (which describes
        the confidence in that specification).

Uncertainty radius in kilometers. For point geometries, indicates
        how far the true location might be from the stated coordinates.
        For polygons, indicates boundary uncertainty. Can be multiple values
        for heterogeneous geometries.
Human-readable label for the property (e.g. 'population').
Review status: 'suggested', 'confirmed', 'rejected'.

Links an Attestation to a Geometry it asserts for the SpatialEntity. An
        attestation may assert multiple geometries (e.g., point and polygon)
        or no geometry at all (e.g., name-only attestations from textual sources).
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes associated with this SpatialEntity.

Timestamp when this attestation was created. This is the contribution
        date, not the historical timespan being attested (use attests_timespan
        for that).

        Semantically equivalent to PROV-O's prov:generatedAtTime. We don't use
        formal rdfs:subPropertyOf to avoid importing PROV-O constraints.

International Phonetic Alphabet representation of the name's
        pronunciation. Enables phonetic search and comparison across scripts
        and languages.

Website or profile URL for the contributor (personal website,
        institutional page, project page, GitHub profile, etc.). Provides
        additional context about the contributor's work and identity.

The transliteration/romanization system used (e.g., 'Pinyin' for
        Chinese, 'BGN/PCGN' for Arabic, 'ISO 259' for Hebrew, 'Hepburn' for
        Japanese). Enables proper interpretation and comparison of romanized
        forms.
The second SpatialEntity in an identity assertion.
The stable, persistent identifier for this SpatialEntity.

ORCID identifier for person contributors. Can be provided in two formats:

        1. Compact format: 0000-0000-0000-0000 (sixteen digits in groups of four)
        2. URI format: https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000 (preferred)

        The URI format (https://orcid.org/...) is preferred and required for
        proper linked data representation. ORCID is particular about always
        including the https:// protocol and domain prefix.

        While optional in the general ontology, specific implementations
        (e.g., WHG) may require ORCID for person contributors to ensure
        proper attribution and citation.

        ORCID provides persistent identification for researchers, enabling
        proper credit and reducing name ambiguity.

Bounding box as array: [min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat].
        Enables fast spatial filtering. Format: comma-separated string
        or JSON array depending on serialization context.

Links an Attestation to a second SpatialEntity, asserting a relationship
        between the Attestation's subject entity (via attests_about) and this
        target entity. The semantic nature of the relationship is specified by
        plato:has_relation_type, which references a RelationType authority.

        Example: An attestation about Constantinople that relates_to the
        Byzantine Empire with relation_type "capital_of" asserts that
        "Constantinople was the capital of the Byzantine Empire".

Free-text organizational affiliation when a structured Organization
        entity is not available. Example: "University of Pittsburgh,
        Institute for Spatial History Innovation"
Version identifier for tracking upstream authority updates.
